4.28.m: Of one who offers himself into her water, sins are destroyed at once;
the attainment of great welfare occurs from that very moment.
Where waters offered with faith to the ancestors by their descendants
provide supreme satisfaction for three autumns, O Acyuta.
She delivers mortals traversing the earth, and reptiles living below,
and in heaven the residents of heaven; therefore she is the Gaṅgā of Viṣṇu that traverses the three worlds.
She is the best sacred ford among sacred fords, the best river among rivers,
bestowing heaven on all creatures, even on those guilty of great sins.

Destroying sins when remembered, Sītā, a raft upon the ocean of worldly existence,

4.29.m:
There indeed the Gaṅgā, who flows along three paths, is present, O sage.
One seeking the good obtains the good; one desiring wealth obtains wealth;
A desirous person obtains desires; one seeking liberation will attain liberation.
From reciting it at the three junctures of the day for a year with faith and a pure mind,
Approaching [his wife] during the fertile season, a childless man will become endowed with sons.
He suffers no untimely death, nor any fear of fire, thieves, or snakes,
Whoever recites the Thousand Names of Gaṅgā with faith, O sage.
Having recited the Thousand Names of Gaṅgā, if one sets out for another village,
He accomplishes his undertaking and returns home free from obstacles.
No defect of lunar days, solar days, asterisms, or astrological yogas can prevail
When a man sets out for another village after reciting this hymn.
It produces longevity and health; it destroys all afflictions;
The Thousand Names of Gaṅgā produces all perfections for men.
Whatever sin has been thoroughly accumulated over thousands of other births,
Through reciting the Thousand Names of Gaṅgā, it goes to destruction.

4.29.m:
A killer of a brahmin, a drinker of liquor, a thief of gold, a defiler of the guru's bed,
One associated with them, a slayer of an embryo, a killer of a mother, a killer of a father, O sage,
A betrayer of trust, a poisoner, an ungrateful person, a slayer of a friend,
An arsonist, a killer of a cow, a stealer of the guru's property—
Even one bound by great sins, or entangled in minor sins,
is freed by reciting with faith the thousand names of the Gaṅgā. (83)
Beset by mental distress and bodily disease, overwhelmed by terrible suffering,
one is released from all sorrows by chanting this hymn. (84)
Concentrated in mind, devoted to worship, reading it for a year,
one attains desired perfection and is completely freed from all sins. (85)
Even of one whose mind is overcome by doubt, or who hates righteousness,
even of an ostentatious or violent person, the mind becomes devoted to virtue. (86)
Walking the path of the castes and stages of life, free from desire and anger,
whatever reward the wise person attains, one gains that through chanting this. (87)
Whatever fruit is acquired by reciting the Gāyatrī ten thousand times,
one fully obtains all of that from a single proper recitation. (88)

4.29.m:
Whatever fruit a righteous man attains by gifting a cow to one learned in the Veda,
that merit is rightly declared [to come] from a single recitation of the king of hymns. (89)
Whatever merit the best of men earns by serving his guru throughout life,
one shares in that by reciting [this hymn] at the three junctions of the day for a year. (190)
Whatever merit is recited here as stemming from a complete reading of the Vedas,
that one attains in six months by proclaiming [it] at the three twilights. (91)
From daily cultivation of this king of hymns to the Gaṅgā,
one attains devotion to Śiva, or becomes a devotee of Viṣṇu. (92)
Whoever proclaims daily the thousand names of the Gaṅgā,
goddess Gaṅgā becomes his constant companion by his side. (93)
He is honored everywhere, he becomes victorious everywhere,
he finds happiness everywhere through the recitation of the hymn to Jāhnavī. (94)
He is to be recognized as one of virtuous conduct, and indeed always pure;
he has performed the worship of all the gods, who recites this praise. (95)
When he is satisfied, Jāhnavī is satisfied—there is no doubt in this;

Whoever hears this king of hymns to Gaṅgā, or recites it,

In whose house this hymn is written down and worshipped,
there is no fear of sin; that home is always pure. (4)
O Agastya, what is the use of saying much? Hear my definitive word:
no doubt should be harbored here, [for] for a doubter there is no fruit.
As many hymns and manifold webs of mantras as exist among mortals, (5)
all of them are not equal to the king of hymns belonging to Gaṅgā. (6)
Whoever recites this thousand of names for as long as he lives,
even if he dies among the Kīkaṭas, he will not enter a womb again. (7)
He who, observing his vows, constantly recites this supreme hymn,
even if he dies elsewhere, has died on the bank of the Gaṅgā. (8)
This excellent, charming hymn was formerly spoken by Pinākin
to Viṣṇu, his own devotee—the vessel of the seed-syllables of liberation. (9)
This hymn has been declared by me as a substitute for ritual ablution in the Gaṅgā;
therefore, desiring to bathe in Jāhnavī, a wise man should recite this hymn. (210)

4.29.m:
Agastya said:
Without bathing in the Gaṅgā, the life of men is futile.
Is there any other means by which one may obtain the fruit of that bath? / 1
And for the incapacitated, the crippled, those crippled by indolence,
and those residing in distant lands, how can a bath in the Gaṅgā take place? / 2
Whether gift, vow, mantra, recitation of praise,
ablution at another sacred ford, or worship of a deity— / 3
if there is anything, O six-faced one, that grants the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā
merely through another ritual procedure, tell that to me who am bowed before you. / 4
No other than you, Skanda, born from the womb of the Gaṅgā,
knows the supreme majesty of the celestial river, O high-minded one. / 5
Skanda said:
There are lakes and rivers here with holy waters, O sage,
and sacred fords in place after place inhabited by self-subdued sages, / 6
which produce visible results and possess great majesty;
yet not even a ten-millionth part of the celestial river is found there. / 7
By this very inference, understand, O pitcher-born one:
the Gaṅgā was borne upon his head by Śambhu, the God of gods. / 8
At the time of bathing in other sacred fords, the Jāhnavī is chanted by people;
apart from the river born of Viṣṇu's foot, where else is anything capable of releasing sin? / 9
The fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā, O brahmin, is obtained only in the Gaṅgā,
just as the taste of a grape fruit is in the grape itself and nowhere else. / 10
Yet there is one means here, O sage, by which the complete fruit
of bathing in the river of the gods may be attained; it is an utter secret: / 11
To a devotee of Śiva, peaceful, devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu,
full of faith, orthodox, and desirous of liberation from dwelling in the womb, / 12
it should be told, and never to anyone else, by anyone, anywhere.
This is the supreme secret, destroying great sins, / 13
bestowing great welfare, auspicious, granting desires, supreme,
producing the love of the heavenly river, a continuity of Śiva's delight, / 14
the thousand names of the Gaṅgā, glorious among the king of praises...

Oṃ, homage to the goddess Gaṅgā!

Embodiment of all deities, gentle, composed of nectar,
Subduer of the snare of ignorance, granter of a state beyond reasoning,
Destroyer of all obstacles, strung with all virtues,
Light in the darkness of ignorance, dedicated to grace,
Delightful, of faultless limbs, of infinite essence, unstained,
Granter of health, vine of bliss, destroyer of the distress of the afflicted,

Refreshing, known as possessed of wisdom, joyful, giver of consolation,
Destroyer of indolence, killer of misfortunes, raining the nectar of bliss,

Skanda said:
On the shore of the southern ocean, near Setubandha,
there was a merchant named Dhanañjaya, endowed with devotion to his mother.
His wealth was acquired through righteous ways, and by his wealth he satisfied seekers.
His fame was spread wide by petitioners, and he was a worshipper of the son of Yaśodā.
Though exceedingly elevated by fortune, his neck was bowed low in humility.
A mine of virtues, he concealed his form among the virtuous.
Though eminent in the beauty of his form, he turned his face away from the wives of others.
Possessed of all accomplishments, his rising was ever spotless, like a full moon free of blemishes.
Though having commerce of mixed truth and falsehood, he was mostly fond of truth, O sage.
Though belonging to a caste other [than the highest], he was praised by all with gold in the world.
Covering the path of good conduct, travelling in comfortable carriages, he was capable.
Though not poor, that intelligent man was impoverished in mind with respect to sin.
While he was living in this manner, once, in the course of time,
his mother met her end, being afflicted with disease and suffering from extreme old age.
And she, having reached youth, which is fleeting as the shadow of a cloud,
like the flood of a rainy-season river, her own husband was deceived.

This city of Kāśī, O brahmin, is the supreme, manifest body of Rudra,

I know its essential truth, or one dedicated to devotion to Śiva [knows it];

This Kāśī is the highest state; this city is supreme bliss;

or the fool who acts maliciously toward the city—he has no refuge either here or elsewhere.
